SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r4#5/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r4#5/r3.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r4#5/r3.claim: Al-Kahf ends by calling humans highly argumentative because its surrounding passages feature dialogue and disputation, including the garden companions, Moses and the righteous servant, and the deniers; al-Isra has no such dialogue or jadal.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r4#5/r3.anchor: أما آية الكهف فقد ختمها بقوله: {وَكَانَ الإنسان أَكْثَرَ شَيْءٍ جَدَلاً}

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p184/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p184/r7.speaker: ثعلب
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p184/r7.claim: Thaʿlab glosses adḥaḍa al-ḥaqq as rendering truth ineffectual; the image comes from a foot slipping on mud.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p184/r7.anchor: أدحض الحق أرهقه قاله ثعلب، وأصله من إدحاض القدم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p184/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p184/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p184/r8.claim: Two cited poems use the root adḥaḍ of a camel slipping on slippery ground.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p184/r8.anchor: وحاد كما حاد البعير عن الدحض

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: The Qur’an mercifully presents truth in varied ways, yet its opponents insist on torment and scourge instead of accepting mercy.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: The Qur’ ān that is being read out to them is a great mercy for them. It is presenting before them the reality in various styles so that they can truly appreciate it.

BURSEVI:v5p199#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p199#2/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p199#2/r1.claim: God swears that He has repeated and varied many forms and arrangements for people's benefit, including the two-gardens parable, worldly-life examples, and calls to faith.
BURSEVI:v5p199#2/r1.anchor: أقسم قسما لقد كررنا وأدرنا على وجوه كثيرة من النظم

BURSEVI:v5p199#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p199#2/r2.speaker: الكاشفي
BURSEVI:v5p199#2/r2.claim: Al-Kashifi says people need examples from past stories to learn and proofs of divine power to deepen insight.
BURSEVI:v5p199#2/r2.anchor: ازهر مثل بران محتاجند از قصص كذشته

BURSEVI:v5p199#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p199#2/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p199#2/r3.claim: Human beings are more argumentative than other creatures capable of dispute; here the term means fierce argument for falsehood, though argument itself need not be false, and its root suggests twisting against an opponent.
BURSEVI:v5p199#2/r3.anchor: وإلا فالجدل لا يلزم أن يكون بالباطل

BURSEVI:v5p199#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p199#2/r4.speaker: أبو أمامة
BURSEVI:v5p199#2/r4.claim: A prophetic report transmitted by Abu Umama says a people do not stray after guidance except that they are given disputation; it is cited from Abu al-Layth's commentary.
BURSEVI:v5p199#2/r4.anchor: وفي الحديث "ما ضل قوم بعد هدى كانوا عليه إلا أوتوا الجدل" رواه أبو أمامة

BURSEVI:v5p199#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p199#2/r5.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
BURSEVI:v5p199#2/r5.claim: The inward reading says argument blocks people's own path: they dispute prophecy, scripture, legal and ambiguous passages, abrogation, interpretation, revelation occasions, readings, and scripture's createdness, never reaching action, obedience, or communion.
BURSEVI:v5p199#2/r5.anchor: قال في "التأويلات النجمية" من طبيعة الإنسان المجادلة والمخاصمة

ALUSI-FULL:v15p299#3/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p299#3/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p299#3/r1.claim: صرفنا means that God repeated the material and presented it in many forms of expression in the Qurʾān for people's benefit.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p299#3/r1.anchor: كررنا وأوردنا على وجوه كثيرة من النظم

ALUSI-FULL:v15p299#3/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p299#3/r2.speaker: الأخفش
ALUSI-FULL:v15p299#3/r2.claim: On al-Akhfash's analysis, من is extra in من كل مثل and the phrase is the direct object of صرفنا.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p299#3/r2.anchor: على أن من سيف خطيب على رأي الأخفش والمجرور مفعول

ALUSI-FULL:v15p299#3/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p299#3/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p299#3/r3.claim: Alternatively, من is partitive and an omitted مثلا described by من كل مثل is the object, or the object is the content of the phrase, meaning examples from each needed category.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p299#3/r3.anchor: أو مثلا من كل مثل على أن من أصلية والمفعول موصوف الجار والمجرور المحذوف

ALUSI-FULL:v15p299#3/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p299#3/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p299#3/r4.claim: مثل may mean familiar parables or striking qualities attractive to the soul; the point is that God varied useful examples that invite faith, not that He listed every possible parable.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p299#3/r4.anchor: فالمراد من المثل إما معناه المشهور أو الصفة الغريبة التي هي في الحسن واستجلاب النفس كالمثل

ALUSI-FULL:v15p299#3/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p299#3/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p299#3/r5.claim: The verse implies that God provided these examples so people would accept faith, though they did not.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p299#3/r5.anchor: وكأن في الآية حذفا أو هي على معنى ولقد فعلنا ذلك ليقبلوا فلم يفعلوا

ALUSI-FULL:v15p300/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p300/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p300/r1.claim: By its nature, the human being is exceptionally argumentative; in this context جدل means contentious, false disputation, while its root evokes twisting and bending one's opponent.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p300/r1.anchor: وهو كما قال الراغب وغيره المنازعة بمفاوضة القول والأليق بالمقام أن يراد به هنا

ALUSI-FULL:v15p300/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p300/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p300/r2.claim: جدلا is accusative as a specification: the human's arguing exceeds that of every other disputant; this is attributed to a volatile range between angelic heights and animal depths.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p300/r2.anchor: وانتصابه على التمييز والمعنى أن جدل الإنسان أكثر من جدل كل مجادل

ALUSI-FULL:v15p300/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p300/r3.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v15p300/r3.claim: Some identify the argumentative human as al-Naḍr ibn al-Ḥārith or Ibn al-Zibʿarī; Ibn al-Sāʾib names Ubayy ibn Khalaf, who challenged resurrection with a crumbled bone.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p300/r3.anchor: وقيل المراد به النضر بن الحرث وقيل ابن الزبعري وقال ابن السائب أبي بن خلف

ALUSI-FULL:v15p300/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p300/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p300/r4.claim: The author prefers the general meaning of humanity, supported by the sound report that the Prophet applied the verse after ʿAlī's reply about their souls being in God's hand.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p300/r4.anchor: والأول أولى ويؤيده ما أخرجه الشيخان وابن المنذر وابن أبي حاتم عن علي

ALUSI-FULL:v15p300/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p300/r5.speaker: علي
ALUSI-FULL:v15p300/r5.claim: ʿAlī reports that when the Prophet urged him and Fāṭima to pray at night, he answered that God held their souls and would raise them if He wished; the Prophet struck his thigh and recited this verse.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p300/r5.anchor: إنما أنفسنا بيد الله تعالى إن شاء أن يبعثنا بعثنا فانصرف حين قلت ذلك

ALUSI-FULL:v15p300/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p300/r6.speaker: النووي
ALUSI-FULL:v15p300/r6.claim: Al-Nawawī says the Prophet struck his thigh from amazement at the quick answer and its refusal to accept his exhortation as an excuse; another view treats the Prophet as accepting their excuse.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p300/r6.anchor: حيث قال المختار في معناه أنه صلى الله عليه وسلم تعجب من سرعة جوابه وعدم موافقته له

ALUSI-FULL:v15p300/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p300/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p300/r7.claim: The author finds the report clearly supports a general reading but says it raises an unresolved difficulty that reflection does not remove.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p300/r7.anchor: إلا أن فيه إشكالا يعرف بالتأمل ولا يدفعه ما ذكره النووي

ALUSI-FULL:v15p310/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p310/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p310/r3.claim: Humans are especially disputatious because they manifest diverse divine names and are a microcosm containing the macrocosm.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p310/r3.anchor: لأنه مظهر الأسماء المختلفة والعالم الأصغر الذي انطوى فيه العالم الأكبر

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p181/r10.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p181/r10.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p181/r10.claim: God has explained every kind of parable in the Qur'an so people may remember and take warning.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p181/r10.anchor: قوله عز وجل: {ولقد صرفنا} بينا {في هذا القرآن للناس من كل مثل} أي ليتذكروا ويتعظوا

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p181/r11.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p181/r11.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p181/r11.claim: Human beings are especially argumentative in falsehood.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p181/r11.anchor: وكان الإنسان أكثر شيء جدلا} خصومة في الباطل.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p181/r12.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p181/r12.speaker: ابن عباس
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p181/r12.claim: Ibn Abbas says the verse targets al-Nadr ibn al-Harith and his disputation about the Qur'an.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p181/r12.anchor: قال ابن عباس: أراد النضر بن الحارث وجداله في القرآن.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p181/r13.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p181/r13.speaker: الكلبي
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p181/r13.claim: Al-Kalbi says the intended person is Ubayy ibn Khalaf al-Jumahi.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p181/r13.anchor: قال الكلبي: أراد به أبي بن خلف الجمحي (2) .

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p181/r14.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p181/r14.speaker: قيل
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p181/r14.claim: One view limits the reference to disbelievers, linking it to their false disputation in 18:56.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p181/r14.anchor: وقيل: المراد من الآية الكفار، لقوله تعالى: "ويجادل الذين كفروا بالباطل"

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p181/r15.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p181/r15.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p181/r15.claim: The author prefers the general reading: the verse describes human beings broadly as argumentative.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p181/r15.anchor: وقيل: هي على العموم، وهذا أصح.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p182/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p182/r1.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p182/r1.claim: Ali reports that the Prophet visited him and Fatima at night to urge prayer; after Ali replied that their souls were in God's hand, the Prophet departed, struck his thigh, and recited the verse about human argumentativeness.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p182/r1.anchor: ثم سمعته وهو مول يضرب فخذه وهو يقول: {وكان الإنسان أكثر شيء جدلا}

BAYDAWI-FULL:18:54-55/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:18:54-55/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:18:54-55/r1.claim: The Quran gives people every kind of example they need.

BAYDAWI-FULL:18:54-55/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:18:54-55/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:18:54-55/r2.claim: Human beings are especially capable of disputation, here meaning false contention; jadal is accusative as a specification.

BIQAI-FULL:v4p481/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p481/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p481/r2.claim: The Quran turns its parables through every meaning and style, with eloquent expressions that distinguish truths and should be widely accepted, yet people still dispute.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p481/r2.anchor: أي حولنا الكلام وطرقناه في كل وجه من وجوه المعاني وألبسناه من العبارات الرائقة

BIQAI-FULL:v4p481/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p481/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p481/r3.claim: Humans are especially contentious because they are naturally self-attached; they continue arguing after the Quran's clarifying proofs.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p481/r3.anchor: وكان الإنسان } الذي جعل خصيما وهو آنس بنفسه جبلة وطبعا { أكثر شيء } وميز الأكثرية

DURR-FULL:v5p404/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p404/r10.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v5p404/r10.claim: The Prophet woke Ali and Fatima to pray; after Ali said their souls were in God's hand, the Prophet left and struck his thigh while reciting that people are highly disputatious.
DURR-FULL:v5p404/r10.anchor: عن علي رضي الله عنه: أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم طرقه وفاطمة ليلا فقال: ألا تصليان فقلت: يا رسول الله

DURR-FULL:v5p406/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p406/r1.speaker: ابن زيد
DURR-FULL:v5p406/r1.claim: In Quranic usage, disputation means people quarrelling with their prophets and rejecting their religious message.
DURR-FULL:v5p406/r1.anchor: عن ابن زيد في قوله: {وكان الإنسان أكثر شيء جدلا} قال: الجدل الخصومة خصومة القوم لآنبيائهم

QUSHAYRI:v2p223/r11.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p223/r11.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p223/r11.claim: Arguments were made clear to everyone, but some were confused and went astray.
QUSHAYRI:v2p223/r11.anchor: أوضح للكافة الحجج ، ولكن لبس على قوم النهج

QUSHAYRI:v2p223/r12.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p223/r12.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p223/r12.claim: Debating against God's enemies can be praiseworthy, but disputing with God implies resistance to decree and is shirk; a believer's good fortune is being opened to action and spared argument.
QUSHAYRI:v2p223/r12.anchor: الجدل في الله محمود مع أعدائه ، والجدل مع الله شرك

QUSHAYRI:v2p223/r13.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p223/r13.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p223/r13.claim: They are not helped toward obedience, yet are neither simply capable nor helpless: if they willed what was commanded it would be withheld; this intermediate state is called takhliya.
QUSHAYRI:v2p223/r13.anchor: وهذا يسميه القوم حال التخلية وهي واسطة بين القدرة والعجز

IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p346/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p346/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p346/r1.claim: The examples continue earlier parables in 18:32 and 18:45; after showing their persuasive force, the passage praises Quranic guidance, recalling 18:27 and 18:29.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p346/r1.anchor: عطف على الجمل السابقة التي ضربت فيها أمثال من قوله : { واضرب لهم مثلا رجلين ( الكهف : 32 )

IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p346/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p346/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p346/r2.claim: Putting في هذا القرآن before للناس, unlike 17:89, foregrounds the Quran because the passage commends its truth rather than human desires.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p346/r2.anchor: إذ قدم هنا قوله : في هذا القرآن } على قوله : { للناس } عكس آية سورة الإسراء

IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p346/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p346/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p346/r3.claim: الناس generally includes everyone who receives the Quran in future ages, while the immediate target is the polytheists; this is general wording shaped by a particular context.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p346/r3.anchor: والناس : اسم عام لكل من يبلغه القرآن في سائر العصور المستقبلة ، والمقصود على الخصوص المشركون

IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p346/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p346/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p346/r4.claim: The closing statement about human argumentation implies that the audience disputed the Quran; الإنسان names the human species and is broader than الناس.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p346/r4.anchor: والتقدير : فجادلوا فيه وكان الإنسان أكثر جدلا ، فإن الإنسان اسم لنوع بني آدم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p346/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p346/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p346/r5.claim: Human argument can be blameworthy, which Islamic discipline restrains, or praiseworthy: Abraham's debate about Lot's people is praised in 11:74–75.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p346/r5.anchor: ومنه محمود كما في قوله تعالى : { فلما ذهب عن إبراهيم الروع وجاءته البشرى يجادلنا في قوم لوط

IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p346/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p346/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p346/r6.claim: The verse does not mean only unbelievers, as in 19:66, or define all argument as false argument, which is specified in 18:56; it prepares for that later charge.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p346/r6.anchor: وليس المراد بالإنسان الإنسان الكافر كما في قوله تعالى : يقول الإنسان أإذا ما مت

IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p347/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p347/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p347/r1.claim: شيء is an indefinite, comprehensive singular, making the superlative construction grammatically sound; here the superlative intensifies rather than compares.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p347/r1.anchor: و ( شيء ) اسم مفرد متوغل في العموم . ولذلك صحت إضافة اسم التفضيل إليه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p347/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p347/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p347/r2.claim: Humans are intensely argumentative even where silence would be better; nonhuman earthly kinds cannot debate, and the wording does not intend comparison with devils or jinn.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p347/r2.anchor: لقصد المبالغة في شدة جدل الإنسان وجنوحه إلى المماراة والنزاع

IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p347/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p347/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p347/r3.claim: Angels' debate can be praiseworthy, as in their question and declaration in 2:30; the author rejects taking the superlative as a literal comparison with jinn or devils.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p347/r3.anchor: أما الملائكة فجدلهم محمود مثل قولهم : أتجعل فيها من يفسد فيها إلى قوله : ونقدس لك

IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p347/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p347/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p347/r4.claim: جدلا is an accusative specification of the relation: humans are numerous in argument, meaning that their arguing is abundant.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p347/r4.anchor: وجدلا } تمييز لنسبة الأكثرية إلى الإنسان . والمعنى : وكان الإنسان كثيرا من جهة الجدل

IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p347/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p347/r5.speaker: علي
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p347/r5.claim: A sound report says the Prophet woke ʿAlī and Fāṭima at night to pray; ʿAlī answered that God controls their souls and would wake them if He willed.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p347/r5.anchor: ما ثبت في ( الصحيح ) عن علي : ( أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم طرقه وفاطمة ليلا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p347/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p347/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p347/r6.claim: The Prophet left without replying, then struck his thigh and recited the verse; Ibn ʿĀshūr says ʿAlī should have welcomed the wake-up and its reproach rather than use it to defend sleeping.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p347/r6.anchor: ثم سمعته يضرب فخذه ويقول : { وكان الإنسان أكثر شيء جدلا }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p347/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p347/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p347/r7.claim: He rejects a literal ranking of humans above jinn and devils in debate, since that is not intended here and their capacity to debate is unestablished.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p347/r7.anchor: ولا يحسن أن يحمل التفضيل في الآية على بابه بأن يرد أن الإنسان أكثر جدلا

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p524/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p524/r8.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p524/r8.claim: God varied warnings and hopes and explained matters through examples useful for guidance; despite this, people turn aside and dispute falsely.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p524/r8.anchor: المعنى: ولقد خوفنا ورجينا وبالغنا في البيان، وهذا كله بتمثيل وتقريب للأذهان،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p524/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p524/r9.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p524/r9.claim: “Humankind” is generic; disputation is verbal contention, and humans are more contentious than any beings they might dispute with, including angels and jinn.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p524/r9.anchor: وقوله الإنسان يريد الجنس، وروي أن سبب هذه الآية هو النضر بن الحارث،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p524/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p524/r10.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p524/r10.claim: Reports name al-Naḍr b. al-Harith or Ibn al-Zabʿari as the occasion; another says the Prophet woke ʿAli after night prayer and repeated the verse after ʿAli said his soul was in God’s hand; Ibn ʿAṭiyya applies it generally.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p524/r10.anchor: وروي أن سبب هذه الآية هو النضر بن الحارث، وقيل ابن الزبعرى. وروي أن رسول الله

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p157/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p157/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p157/r1.claim: The Quran’s varied examples were discussed at 17:41.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p157/r1.anchor: قوله تعالى ولقد صرفنا في هذا القرآن قد فسرناه في بني اسرائيل

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p157/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p157/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p157/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas says the verse concerned al-Nadr ibn al-Harith, who disputed the Quran.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p157/r2.anchor: انه النضر بن الحارث وكان جداله في القرآن قاله ابن عباس

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p157/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p157/r3.speaker: ابن السائب
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p157/r3.claim: Ibn al-Saʾib says it concerned Ubayy ibn Khalaf, who disputed resurrection after bringing a decayed bone and asking whether God could restore it.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p157/r3.anchor: أبي بن خلف وكان جداله في البعث حين أتى بعظم قد رم فقال أيقدر الله على إعادة هذا

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p157/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p157/r4.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p157/r4.claim: Al-Zajjaj says angels and jinn, like all rational beings, argue, but humans argue more than any of them.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p157/r4.anchor: كل ما يعقل من الملائكة والجن يجادل والإنسان أكثر هذه الأشياء جدلا

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p171#2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p171#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p171#2/r1.claim: God has explained and clarified matters through varied Quranic examples to keep people from leaving guidance, yet humans argue excessively and oppose truth with falsehood, except those God guides.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p171#2/r1.anchor: بينا للناس في هذا القرآن، ووضحنا لهم الأمور، وفصلناها

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p171#2/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p171#2/r2.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p171#2/r2.claim: When the Prophet urged ʿAlī and Fāṭima to pray at night, ʿAlī excused them by saying their souls were in God's hand; the Prophet left and recited this verse while striking his thigh. Both Ṣaḥīḥ collections record it.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p171#2/r2.anchor: أن علي بن أبي طالب أخبره، أن رسول الله (2) صلى الله عليه وسلم طرقه

JISHUMI:v6p4440/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4440/r6.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p4440/r6.claim: Jidāl is disputation, with a root sense of firmness; an ajdal is a strong falcon.
JISHUMI:v6p4440/r6.anchor: والجدال: الخصومة، وأصله الشدة، ومنه: الأجدل: الصقر لشدته.

JISHUMI:v6p4440/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4440/r8.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p4440/r8.claim: Akthar is the predicate of kāna, while jadalan is accusative as a specification.
JISHUMI:v6p4440/r8.anchor: أكثر نصب لأنه خبر (كان). جدلا نصب على التفسير والتمييز.

JISHUMI:v6p4440/r9.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4440/r9.speaker: الكلبي
JISHUMI:v6p4440/r9.claim: The verse about human disputation was revealed concerning Ubayy ibn Khalaf; al-Kalbi identifies the people as Meccans.
JISHUMI:v6p4440/r9.anchor: قيل: نزل قوله: وكان الإنسان أكثر شيء جدلا في أبي بن خلف الجمحي، قال الكلبي: أراد بالناس أهل مكة

JISHUMI:v6p4440/r12.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4440/r12.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p4440/r12.claim: The Qur’an varies and repeats examples so people will reflect.
JISHUMI:v6p4440/r12.anchor: قيل: تصريفها ترديدها من نوع واحد وأنواع مختلفة ليتفكروا فيها

JISHUMI:v6p4440/r13.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4440/r13.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p4440/r13.claim: Humankind is especially prone to arguing falsely.
JISHUMI:v6p4440/r13.anchor: وكان الإنسان أكثر شيء جدلا خصومة بالباطل

JISHUMI:v6p4442/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4442/r2.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p4442/r2.claim: Repeated examples invite reflection and validate religious reasoning while condemning blind imitation.
JISHUMI:v6p4442/r2.anchor: وتدل على أنه صرف الآيات ليتفكر فيها، فتدل على صحة الحجاج في الدين، وحسن النظر، وذم التقليد.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p680#3/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p680#3/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p680#3/r1.claim: Humans are more argumentative than any other thing capable of argument, taken one by one; their dispute is contention and false wrangling, with jadalan in the accusative as specification.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p680#3/r1.anchor: أكثر الأشياء التي يتأتى منها الجدل إن فصلتها واحدا بعد واحد ، خصومة ومماراة بالباطل

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p680#3/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p680#3/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p680#3/r2.claim: The construction is like ‘then he is a clear disputant.’
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p680#3/r2.anchor: ونحوه : { فإذا هو خصيم مبين } ( النحل : 4 )

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p317#2/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p317#2/r1.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p317#2/r1.claim: The Qur'an's varied examples may be lessons from earlier peoples, warning people about their fate.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p317#2/r1.anchor: أحدهما : ما ذكره لهم من العبر في القرون الخالية . الثاني : ما أوضحه لهم من دلائل الربوبية

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p317#2/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p317#2/r2.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p317#2/r2.claim: Alternatively, the examples clarify proofs of God's lordship, making the passage an exposition.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p317#2/r2.anchor: ما أوضحه لهم من دلائل الربوبية , فيكون على الوجه الأول جزاء , وعلى الثاني بيانا .

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p317#2/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p317#2/r3.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p317#2/r3.claim: Human contentiousness can mean obstinacy, fitting the first interpretation of the examples.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p317#2/r3.anchor: أحدهما : عنادا , وهو مقتضى الوجه الأول .

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p317#2/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p317#2/r4.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p317#2/r4.claim: Alternatively, it means argumentation, fitting the second interpretation.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p317#2/r4.anchor: الثاني : حجاجا وهو مقتضى القول الثاني .

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p317#2/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p317#2/r5.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p317#2/r5.claim: A report says the Prophet found Ali and Fatima asleep, called them to pray, heard Ali say their souls were in God's control, then left reciting this verse.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p317#2/r5.anchor: روي أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم دخل على علي وفاطمة رضي الله عنهما وهما نائمان فقال :

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p317#2/r6.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p317#2/r6.speaker: علي
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p317#2/r6.claim: Ali replied that their souls belonged to God and He would awaken them whenever He wished.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p317#2/r6.anchor: فقال علي رضي الله عنه : إنما أنفسنا بيد الله فإذا شاء أن يبعثها بعثها ,

MUQATIL:18:52-54/r5.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:18:52-54/r5.speaker: author
MUQATIL:18:52-54/r5.claim: Ṣarrafnā means varied or described: the Qur'an presents likenesses about diverse matters.
MUQATIL:18:52-54/r5.anchor: يعني لونا، يعني وصفنا، { في هذا القرآن للناس من كل مثل }

MUQATIL:18:52-54/r6.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:18:52-54/r6.speaker: author
MUQATIL:18:52-54/r6.claim: Human beings are especially prone to argument.
MUQATIL:18:52-54/r6.anchor: من كل شبه في أمور شتى، { وكان الإنسان أكثر شيء جدلا }

NASAFI-FULL:v3p18#2/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p18#2/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p18#2/r1.claim: The Qur’an has varied every kind of example people need; humanity is the greatest in disputation and contention with false argument.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p18#2/r1.anchor: ﴿ ولقد صرفنا في هذا القرآن للناس من كل مثل ﴾ يحتاجون اليه ﴿ وكان الإنسان أكثر شيء جدلا ﴾ تمييز أي أكثر الأشياء التي يتأنى منها الجدل

NASAFI-FULL:v3p18#2/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p18#2/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p18#2/r2.claim: جدلا means quarrelling and disputation; human argument exceeds that of every disputing thing considered one by one.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p18#2/r2.anchor: خصومة ومماراة بالباطل يعني أن جدل الإنسان أكثر من جدل كل شيء

QURTUBI-FULL:18:54-56/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:54-56/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:18:54-56/r1.claim: The Quran’s examples either recount instructive histories of past peoples as warning or clarify proofs of divine lordship as exposition.
QURTUBI-FULL:18:54-56/r1.anchor: يحتمل وجهين: أحدهما: ما ذكره لهم من العبر والقرون الخالية.

QURTUBI-FULL:18:54-56/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:54-56/r2.speaker: author والزجاج
QURTUBI-FULL:18:54-56/r2.claim: The argumentative human is identified with al-Nadr ibn al-Harith or Ubayy ibn Khalaf; al-Zajjaj takes it as unbelievers generally. Anas reports an unbeliever’s limbs testifying at Judgment, and Ali reports the Prophet quoting the verse after a nighttime prayer exchange.
QURTUBI-FULL:18:54-56/r2.anchor: والمراد به النضر بن الحارث وجداله في القرآن. وقيل: الآية في أبي بن خلف.

MAJAZ:v1p406/r4.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v1p406/r4.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v1p406/r4.claim: موبقا means an appointment or appointed meeting; the cited line uses it for a meeting place or time.
MAJAZ:v1p406/r4.anchor: «وجعلنا بينهم موبقا» (54) أي موعدا، قال: وحاد شرورى والستار فلم يدع

RAZI-FULL:v21p119#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p119#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p119#2/r1.claim: The repeated examples answer the wealthy Meccan disbelievers' boast and expose their claim as false, yet they persist in futile disputation; taṣrīf signals repetition.
RAZI-FULL:v21p119#2/r1.anchor: التصريف يقتضي التكرير والأمر كذلك لأنه تعالى أجاب عن شبهتهم

RAZI-FULL:v21p119#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p119#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p119#2/r2.claim: In وكان الإنسان أكثر شيء جدلا, جدلا is a tamyīz distinguishing the human as the most argumentative of things capable of disputation.

RAZI-FULL:v21p119#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p119#2/r3.speaker: بعض المحققين
RAZI-FULL:v21p119#2/r3.claim: The verse implies that prophets debated religion with opponents, since disputation necessarily has two sides; this also refutes reliance on imitation alone.
RAZI-FULL:v21p119#2/r3.anchor: قال بعض المحققين والآية دالة على أن الأنبياء عليهم السلام جادلوهم في الدين

STUDYQURAN:18:54/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:18:54/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:18:54/r1.claim: The Quran's many kinds of parables serve human moral and religious instruction.
STUDYQURAN:18:54/r1.anchor: that is, for the moral and religious instruction of human beings

STUDYQURAN:18:54/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:18:54/r2.speaker: Ṭ, Bḍ
STUDYQURAN:18:54/r2.claim: Human beings are contentious because they vainly argue against prophets and messengers on false grounds; the discussion continues in v. 56.
STUDYQURAN:18:54/r2.anchor: vainly opposing and arguing against the prophets and messengers sent to them

TAB-FULL:v15p300/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p300/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v15p300/r1.claim: God has presented people with every kind of example, admonition, and proof in the Qur’an so they may remember, repent, learn, and abandon idolatry.
TAB-FULL:v15p300/r1.anchor: مثلنا في هذا القرآن للناس من كل مثل، ووعظناهم فيه من كل عظة

TAB-FULL:v15p300/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p300/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v15p300/r2.claim: Humans are exceptionally argumentative, persisting in dispute rather than submitting to truth or taking admonition.
TAB-FULL:v15p300/r2.anchor: وكان الإنسان أكثر شيء مراء وخصومة، لا ينيب لحق، ولا ينزجر لموعظة

TAB-FULL:v15p300/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p300/r3.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB-FULL:v15p300/r3.claim: Ibn Zayd defines jadal as disputation against prophets and rejection of their message, illustrated by objections that the messengers are ordinary people or that revelation is impossible.
TAB-FULL:v15p300/r3.anchor: قال ابن زيد، في قوله: {وكان الإنسان أكثر شيء جدلا} [الكهف: 54] قال: الجدل: الخصومة، خصومة القوم لأنبيائهم، وردهم عليهم ما جاءوا به

TABATABAI:18:55-57/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:18:55-57/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:18:55-57/r1.claim: The opening resembles 17:89; the following six verses threaten punishment after the preceding reminders, and jadal means contentious disputation.
TABATABAI:18:55-57/r1.anchor: قد مر الكلام في نظير صدر الآية في سورة الإسراء آيه 89 والجدل الكلام على سبيل المنازعة والمشاجرة

TABRISI:18:53-55/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:18:53-55/r10.speaker: author
TABRISI:18:53-55/r10.claim: The Qur'an gives varied examples in repeated forms to prompt reflection; this was discussed in Sūrat Banī Isrāʾīl.
TABRISI:18:53-55/r10.anchor: تصريفها ترديدها من نوع واحد وأنواع مختلفة ليتفكروا فيها

TABRISI:18:53-55/r11.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:18:53-55/r11.speaker: ابن عباس
TABRISI:18:53-55/r11.claim: The combative person meant by al-insān is al-Naḍr ibn al-Ḥārith.
TABRISI:18:53-55/r11.anchor: يريد بالإنسان النضر بن الحارث عن ابن عباس

TABRISI:18:53-55/r12.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:18:53-55/r12.speaker: الكلبي
TABRISI:18:53-55/r12.claim: The combative person meant by al-insān is Ubayy ibn Khalaf.
TABRISI:18:53-55/r12.anchor: ويريد أبي بن خلف عن الكلبي

TABRISI:18:53-55/r13.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:18:53-55/r13.speaker: الزجاج
TABRISI:18:53-55/r13.claim: Al-insān means unbelievers generally, as the following mention of their disputing with falsehood indicates.
TABRISI:18:53-55/r13.anchor: وقال الزجاج معناه وكأن الكافر يدل عليه قوله

THALABI:v6p178/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p178/r4.speaker: author
THALABI:v6p178/r4.claim: ‘The human is most disputatious’ means persistent argument for falsehood; one view specifies Ubayy ibn Khalaf, another applies it generally.
THALABI:v6p178/r4.anchor: وكان الإنسان أكثر شيء جدلا: خصومة في الباطل، يعني أبي بن خلف الجمحي،

THALABI:v6p178/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p178/r5.speaker: الحسن بن علي عن أبيه
THALABI:v6p178/r5.claim: When the Prophet woke Ali and Fatima for prayer, Ali said their souls were in God’s hand and He would wake them if He wished; the Prophet left repeating this verse and striking his thigh.
THALABI:v6p178/r5.anchor: روى الحسن بن علي بن أبي طالب عن أبيه قال: «إن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم طرقه

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p57/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p57/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p57/r1.claim: The Qurʾān's varied examples were explained in two places in Sūrat Banī Isrāʾīl.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p57/r1.anchor: مفسرا في سورة بني إسرائيل في موضعين

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p57/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p57/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p57/r2.claim: The disputatious human is al-Naḍr ibn al-Ḥārith, whose argument concerned the Qurʾān.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p57/r2.anchor: قال ابن عباس: (يريد النضر بن الحارث، وجداله في القرآن)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p57/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p57/r3.speaker: الكلبي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p57/r3.claim: He identifies the disputatious human as Ubayy ibn Khalaf.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p57/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p57/r4.speaker: أبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p57/r4.claim: Human means the unbeliever generally, as the next verse says; other rational beings also dispute, but humans dispute more than they do.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p57/r4.anchor: معناه كان الكافر، ويدل عليه قوله: {ويجادل الذين كفروا بالباطل}

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:18:52-55/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:18:52-55/r4.speaker: أبي بن خلف
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:18:52-55/r4.claim: One reported identification of the human who is most argumentative is Ubayy ibn Khalaf.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:18:52-55/r4.anchor: وكان الإنسان } الكافر { أكثر شيء جدلا } قيل: هو أبي بن خلف

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:18:52-55/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:18:52-55/r5.speaker: النضر بن الحارث
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:18:52-55/r5.claim: Another reported identification of the human who is most argumentative is al-Nadr ibn al-Harith.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:18:52-55/r5.anchor: جدلا } قيل: هو أبي بن خلف، وقيل: النضر بن الحارث.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p192/r3.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p192/r3.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p192/r3.claim: The Qur'an's varied examples recall 17:89, and the human being who disputes most is the disbeliever arguing about God.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p192/r3.anchor: كقوله: {ولقد صرفنا للناس في هذا القرءان من كل مثل} [الإسراء: 89] .

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p192/r4.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p192/r4.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p192/r4.claim: Most contentious means the disbeliever argues about God.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p192/r4.anchor: {وكان الإنسان أكثر شيء جدلا} [الكهف: 54] يعني: الكافر يجادل في الله.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p192/r5.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p192/r5.speaker: الحسن
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p192/r5.claim: One report says the Prophet found a member of his household asleep, told him to pray, and heard him argue that people pray only as much as decreed; the Prophet cited this verse.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p192/r5.anchor: - الحسن، عن الحسن، قال: أتى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم على بعض أهله وهو نائم، فقال:

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p192/r6.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p192/r6.speaker: الحسن
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p192/r6.claim: Another report says the Prophet nudged a sleeping man in the mosque to pray; the man replied that he prayed only as decreed, and the Prophet cited this verse.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p192/r6.anchor: - أبو الأشهب، عن الحسن، قال: أتى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم على رجل نائم في المسجد فضربه برجله وقال:

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:18:54/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:18:54/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:18:54/r1.claim: God gives many examples—from a mosquito and the vast heavens to worldly transience and good and evil—to prompt reflection and acceptance of truth; stubbornness, denial, selfishness, and self-interest instead drive some to resist revelation and the Prophet.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:18:54/r1.anchor: Allah Teâlâ, insanlar ibret alsınlar diye Kur’an’da çokça misal vermiştir. Sivri sinekten, akıllara durgunluk veren uçsuz bucaksız göklerin yaratılışından, dünya hayatının fâniliğinden

SAMIN-DURR:18:54/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:18:54/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:18:54/r1.claim: من كل may modify an omitted noun that is the object of صرفنا, meaning a parable from every kind; alternatively, Akhfash and the Kufans treat من as extra.

SAMIN-DURR:18:54/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:18:54/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:18:54/r2.claim: جدلا is an accusative specification noun.

SAMIN-DURR:18:54/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:18:54/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:18:54/r3.claim: أكثر شيء means people exceed all disputants in argument when the disputing things are considered individually; singular شيء stands for plural things.
SAMIN-DURR:18:54/r3.anchor: أكثر الأشياء التي يتأتى منها الجدال إن فصلتها واحدا واحدا

SAMIN-DURR:18:54/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:18:54/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:18:54/r4.claim: One possible analysis derives جدلا from the original subject of كان, with the underlying wording “the human’s disputation was the greatest thing”; the author sees difficulty in this.
SAMIN-DURR:18:54/r4.anchor: من اسم كان إذ الأصل: وكان جدل الإنسان أكثر شيء؟ فيه نظر.

SAMIN-DURR:18:54/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:18:54/r5.speaker: أبو البقاء
SAMIN-DURR:18:54/r5.claim: He offers two explanations: شيء means disputant, since a comparative is related to a category it partly belongs to; or omitted wording is جدل الإنسان and جدلا specifies it.
SAMIN-DURR:18:54/r5.anchor: شيئا هنا في معنى مجادل؛ لأن أفعل يضاف إلى ما هو بعض له

SAMIN-DURR:18:54/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:18:54/r6.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:18:54/r6.claim: The second estimate needs a further metaphor: one must attribute disputation to disputation itself, like شعر شاعر, to say human disputation exceeds other disputation.
SAMIN-DURR:18:54/r6.anchor: وهو أن تتجوز فتجعل للجدل جدلا كقولهم:

ZAJJAJ:v3p296/r1.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p296/r1.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p296/r1.claim: The Qur’an has explained every example people need.
ZAJJAJ:v3p296/r1.anchor: أي من كل مثل يحتاجون إليه، أي بيناه لهم

ZAJJAJ:v3p296/r2.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p296/r2.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p296/r2.claim: Al-insān here means the unbeliever, as the following verse says unbelievers dispute falsely; Iblis, angels, and jinn also dispute, but humans are the most argumentative among these beings.
ZAJJAJ:v3p296/r2.anchor: معناه كان الكافر، ويدل عليه قوله: (ويجادل الذين كفروا بالباطل

ASAD-NOTES:18:54#n60/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:18:54#n60/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:18:54#n60/r1.claim: Asad translates mathal as "lesson" here, following his explanation at 17:89.
ASAD-NOTES:18:54#n60/r1.anchor: explaining my translation of mathal, in this context, as "lesson".

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: “Parables” here convey facts about the afterlife and unseen world in forms meant to warn people.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: facts and realities of the hereafter and of the unknown world that are presented in the form of parables

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: “Human” refers to the contentious Quraysh; the general term expresses the author’s aversion to them.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: refers to the quarrelsome Quraysh that are already under discussion. A general word has been used in order to express aversion from them.

QIRAAT-ER:18:54:7#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:18:54:7#1/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:18:54:7#1/r1.claim: Hamza's canonical reading simplifies the hamza in qurʾān, reflecting dialectal pronunciation without a stated semantic difference.
QIRAAT-ER:18:54:7#1/r1.anchor: Hamza simplification: dropping hamza from qurʾān to qurān; attested canonical variant

ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p404#7/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p404#7/r2.speaker: علي بن حسين
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p404#7/r2.claim: Ali ibn al-Husayn recounts that the Prophet urged Ali and Fatima to pray; Ali answered that God held their souls, and the Prophet left reciting that humans are disputatious.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p404#7/r2.anchor: عن الزهري عن علي بن حسين قال دخل النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم على علي وفاطمة وهما نائمان

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p193/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p193/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p193/r1.claim: Here شيء is singular in form but collective in meaning: every possible item of argument is considered one by one; جدلا means disputation and is an accusative of specification.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p193/r1.anchor: وشيء هنا مفرد معناه الجمع أي أكثر الأشياء التي يتأتى منها الجدال

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p193/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p193/r2.speaker: ابن السائب
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p193/r2.claim: Some identify the argumentative human as al-Nadr ibn al-Harith, Ibn al-Zibara, or Ubayy ibn Khalaf; Ibn al-Sa'ib says the dispute concerned resurrection and a crumbled bone.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p193/r2.anchor: قيل: الإنسان هنا النضر بن الحارث. وقيل: ابن الزبعرى. وقيل:

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p193/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p193/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p193/r3.claim: Another view says every rational kind, including angels and jinn, argues, but humans argue more than all the rest.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p193/r3.anchor: قيل: كل من يعقل من ملك وجن يجادل والإنسان أكثر هذه الأشياء جدلا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p193/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p193/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p193/r4.claim: The Prophet recited this verse while admonishing Ali for sleeping through night prayer; Ali replied that his soul is in God's hand, showing الإنسان is generic.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p193/r4.anchor: وقد تلا الرسول صلى الله عليه وسلم قوله: وكان الإنسان أكثر شيء جدلا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p193/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p193/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p193/r5.claim: The Quran often mentions the human being in a blameworthy context.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p193/r5.anchor: وكثيرا ما يذكر الإنسان في معرض الذم

ITQAN:v3p293#3/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p293#3/r6.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p293#3/r6.claim: A Qur’anic pattern pairs the record of deeds shown at judgment with the worldly book of religious rulings that grounds accountability; the Kahf and Isra passages illustrate the pattern.
ITQAN:v3p293#3/r6.anchor: أن عادة القرآن إذا ذكر الكتاب المشتمل على عمل العبد حيث يعرض يوم القيامة أردفه بذكر الكتاب المشتمل على الأحكام الدينية في الدنيا

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r4#5/f2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r4#5/f2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r4#5/f2.claim: Isra places “for people” before “in this Quran,” fitting its prior discussion of people and divine favors; Kahf delays it, matching a sūra that opens with the Quran before its human stories.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r4#5/f2.anchor: قدم (للناس) على (في هذه القرآن) في الإسراء وأخرها في (الكهف)

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r4#5/f4.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r4#5/f4.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r4#5/f4.claim: Kahf's ending about human contentiousness fits its many surrounding disputes: the two companions' dialogue, unbelievers' arguments, Moses' debate, and the instruction not to dispute about the youths.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r4#5/f4.anchor: لما ذكر قبلها وبعدها من المحاورات والجدل والمراء من مثل قوله تعالى

SAMARRAI-ASRAR-MUH:p50/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR-MUH:p50/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR-MUH:p50/r2.claim: Kahf places the Quran before people because the surah opens with the revealed Book, then recounts stories of people, matching the order in the verse.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR-MUH:p50/r2.anchor: فبدأ بذكر القرآن ثم ذكر الناس فكان المناسب أن يتقدم ذكر القرآن على الناس في هذه الآية كما في البدء

SAMARRAI-ASRAR-MUH:p51/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR-MUH:p51/r3.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR-MUH:p51/r3.claim: Kahf’s close about human argument matches its dialogues and disputes, including the garden companions, the disbelievers, and Moses with the righteous servant; Isra contains no such debate language.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR-MUH:p51/r3.anchor: ولم يرد لفظ الجدل ولا المحاورة في سورة الإسراء كلها

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p501/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p501/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p501/r2.claim: Al-Kahf reverses the order because it opens with the Qur'an, then recounts the people and their stories; foregrounding the Book in 18:54 matches that opening.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p501/r2.anchor: فقد بدأ السورة بالكلام على الكتاب وهو القرآن ثم ذكر بعده أصحاب الكهف

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p502/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p502/r3.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p502/r3.claim: Al-Kahf's close about human disputation matches its dialogues and argument: the garden companions, Moses and the righteous man, and disbelievers debating falsely; Al-Isrāʾ lacks this vocabulary.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p502/r3.anchor: ولم يرد لفظ الجدل ولا المحاورة في سورة الإسراء كلها
